correctness.rationale: For all r in (0,1), membership in the F-stochastic class is certified by \(\varphi(x,y)=(x+y)^2/2\) and \(g(t)=t^2/2\), satisfying C1–C3 even at \(t=1\). Composition after one step fixes the survivor fractions, giving \(s_{n+1}=c_{\xi_{n-1}}s_n^2\) exactly for all \(n\ge1\) and all infinite switch strings. Taking logarithms and summing the uniformly absolutely convergent weighted series gives the stated L, support interval and convex-combination tail bound. Cylinder independence proves nonatomic/full support and uniformity at p=1/2; binary digit-frequency strong law proves mutual singularity; cylinder entropy/Frostman estimates prove dimension \(h(p)/\log2\); finite moments are geometric. The actual packaged checker passed exhaustive finite words, exact fractions and high precision tails. All boundary restrictions and unproved generalizations are explicit.

originality.rationale: The three accessible primary open texts were compared by mathematical statement and object. Souissi–Mukhamedov 2024 and Jamilov et al. 2024 prove fixed-operator regularity and associated Markov chain properties. Jamilov et al. 2023 allows independently randomly chosen F-QSOs and proves eventual extinction, not the explicit distribution of the samplewise log-decay exponent. The measure-theory consequences are classical and expressly credited; the identified new contribution is the exact two-sex switched-model reduction and resultant familywide sharp rate-law classification. No exact equivalent or dominating statement was identified in actual research-record queries or accessible local previous claims.
residual_risks: Classical Bernoulli measure formulas may have been applied elsewhere to the same two-sex switched quadratic model under a different name; an exhaustive priority search is impossible.
The closest paper on randomly switched F-QSOs is a general convergence result; unindexed appendices or theses might contain this explicit subfamily.
Some candidate broader Bernoulli-convolution resources were inspected only at abstract level; no whole-document noncoverage inference is made from them.

value.rationale: The samplewise double-exponential extinction rate is a natural sharp asymptotic invariant for randomly varying sex/heredity environments, not an arbitrary numeric slice. The identified law has a full-support uniform/singular transition and pairwise mutually singular laws for distinct environmental probabilities despite identical deterministically extinct equilibrium and identical rate support. Explicit finite-time error, mean and variance improve reproducibility. The statement covers every pair of distinct contraction coefficients and every positive two-type initial composition; it is deliberately not claimed for general F-stochastic operators.
